A document attributed to "Cleopatra the Alchemist", a pseudonym, shows a snake biting its tail, the ouroboros, around the motto: "One is the All".

« Jabir » n'est peut-être pas une seule: "Jabir" may not be one person: most historians see in his corpus the work of an anonymous school, later than the Jabir of tradition.

The corpus also gives the oldest known recipe for obtaining sal ammoniac from organic substances, such as blood or hair.
Le corpus de Jabir (850-950) : soufre et: The Jabirian corpus (850-950): sulfur and mercury make metals, the elixir cures them, the balance measures them.

In chemistry, his Secrets and Secret of Secrets give the first ordered classification of substances, reactions and apparatus, with very little mysticism.

Al-Razi, vers 900 : six familles de miné: Al-Razi, around 900: six families of minerals and an inventory of the laboratory. He still believed in transmutation.
Le mot alchimie vient de l'arabe al-kīmi: The word alchemy comes from Arabic al-kīmiyā; elixir, from al-iksīr. Alchimie, élixir, alcool : des mots arab: Alchemy, elixir, alcohol: Arabic words. "Alcohol" comes from kohl, a powder for the eyes.

The Byzantines kept the secret so well that it was lost; today a petroleum-based mixture is suspected, without certainty.

In India, clay retorts and receivers from the first centuries of our era, the "Gandhara stills", gave only a very weak distillate. In China, it may have begun as early as the Eastern Han, in the 1st and 2nd centuries; a 12th-century still has been found in Hebei.
Le feu grégeois (v. 672) garde son secre: Greek fire (c. 672) keeps its secret. Distillation was practised in India and China from the first centuries.
Au XIIe siècle, des textes latins donnen: In the 12th century, Latin texts gave recipes for aqua ardens, "burning water", drawn from wine distilled with salt. In the 14th century, the alchemist John of Rupescissa saw it as a "quintessence", an imperishable, life-giving fifth essence, and studied its medical virtues. Eau ardente au XIIe siècle ; 90 % d'alco: Burning water in the 12th century; 90% alcohol with Alderotti; aqua vitae gave whiskey, eau-de-vie and akvavit.

Pseudo-Geber, vers 1310 : corpuscules de: Pseudo-Geber, around 1310: corpuscles of sulfur and mercury, nitric acid, aqua regia that dissolves gold.

Biringuccio (Pirotechnia, 1540) et Agric: Biringuccio (Pirotechnia, 1540) and Agricola (De re metallica, 1556) put the knowledge of founders and miners into print.
Paracelse n'est pas un chimiste moderne: Paracelsus was not a modern chemist: he remained an alchemist, astrologer and mystic. What matters is that he brought chemical remedies into medicine.
Theophrastus Bombast von Hohenheim naît: Theophrastus Bombast von Hohenheim was born on 10 November 1493 in Switzerland, at Einsiedeln. He signed himself Paracelsus, a name first attested in 1529, meaning either "high" or "beyond Celsus", the Roman physician. On 23 June 1527, in Basel, he burned Avicenna's Canon, the physicians' bible, in the market square.
